lastText: ☰⚙File ClosedThe Cost of the Other RoadThe Joint Chiefs of Staff, 1940–1945A war that confirmed Europe First at Arcadia, and fought a honestly different middle, a declined Midway ambush, or every Central Pacific atoll taken by direct assault instead of bypassed, converges back toward its historical shape at the finish anyway. The bomb, the Soviet declaration, and Japan's cabinet deadlock land almost exactly when they actually did, largely indifferent to which operational road got the fleet to 1945. What changed, put plainly on the record rather than left in this fleet's own files, sits beside the documented total for this theater, a little over 111,000 American dead: not a different destination, but a real, countable addition to or subtraction from that number, depending on which road actually got walked.The Theater Map at the end of the warPacific Situation · The war as it ended · Theater MapJapan: ContestedFormosa: ContestedManchukuo: ContestedNorth China: ContestedEast China: ContestedGuangdong: ContestedHunan-Guangxi: Allied-controlled / liberatedFree China: Allied-controlled / liberatedYan'an: Allied-controlled / liberatedTibet & Xinjiang: Neutral / not yet contestedIndochina: ContestedThailand: ContestedBurma: Allied-controlled / liberatedIndia: Allied-controlled / liberatedMalaya: ContestedSumatra: ContestedJava: ContestedBorneo: ContestedCelebes: ContestedMoluccas & Timor: ContestedLuzon: Allied-controlled / liberatedVisayas: Allied-controlled / liberatedMindanao: All
